PullRequest.Title: Telemetry: Preserve Copilot telemetry content and structured reasoning metadata
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

- Always emit compressed `messageText` chunks for extension-host and Agent Host telemetry, and add Agent Host `prompt` chunking parity.
- Preserve provider-native reasoning, summaries, and opaque state in extension-host telemetry, with structured metadata describing content purpose, visibility, and format.
- Retain reasoning content from Responses API items and trailing reasoning metadata received after `finish_reason`, including multi-choice responses.
- Keep model requests, displayed answers, tool behavior, and progress callbacks unchanged. Output-content telemetry waits until the stream ends to include trailing metadata.
- Add regression coverage for chunk boundaries, Unicode, native reasoning, trailing metadata, and unchanged completion delivery.

## Validation

- Targeted extension tests via the VS Code test runner: **130 passed**.
- Agent Host chunking:
  `.\scripts\test.bat --run src\vs\platform\agentHost\test\node\agentHostRestrictedTelemetry.test --grep "AgentHost restricted telemetry chunking"` — **11 passed**.
- From `extensions\copilot`:
  `npx --no-install tsc --noEmit --project tsconfig.json` — **passed**.
- `git diff --check` — **passed**.

## Follow-up

- End-to-end conversation-text preservation requires tel ingestion support for `messageTextChunk`.
- Agent Host runtime content classification remains a separate change; this PR preserves forwarded metadata but does not infer classifications in the host router.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The Promise.finally ordering, expanded data shape, synchronous hash/serialization implementation, and downstream stream-start call path are all directly visible. Exact milliseconds vary with history size and telemetry configuration, but the added critical-path work and linear/per-8K scaling are deterministic.
Findings.PerformanceResource: CPU work, large strings, telemetry event objects, and gzip input buffers
Findings.PerformanceScaling: The synchronous work grows with the complete Responses API history: every message is classified and hashed, every new message is JSON-serialized, and one internal event is created per 8,000 characters; deduplication still hashes the full content on every request.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Increased time to start consuming the response stream, plus CPU and allocation/GC pressure on long agent conversations.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: This same finally block converted Responses history through responseApiInputToRawMessagesForLogging/rawMessageToCAPI, which reduced reasoning to a short summary placeholder and omitted compaction and image-generation items before telemetry processing.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The changed line now preserves complete provider-native reasoning, encrypted compaction state, and generated-image data, then passes that expanded history to sendEngineMessagesTelemetry synchronously from the postRequest Promise's finally handler.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 1626 replaces the compact logging conversion with responseApiInputToTelemetryMessages; that converter returns full reasoning/compaction items and image results, and unchanged line 1633 synchronously invokes sendEngineMessagesTelemetry before the postRequest Promise can settle.
Findings.Title: Move native input telemetry off the response-start path
Findings.Impact: A long Responses conversation—especially one carrying reasoning/compaction state or an image-generation result—adds telemetry CPU and allocation latency between receiving headers and reading the first response chunks, delaying first-token display and every subsequent agent model call.
Findings.Evidence: The HTTP request Promise executes this finally block before returning Response to the caller, while stream processing starts only afterward in chatMLFetcher.ts:1442. sendEngineMessagesTelemetry synchronously maps metadata and JSON.stringify's the full array; sendIndividualMessagesTelemetry then recursively hashes every character (hash.ts:stringHash), JSON.stringify's each new message, splits it into 8K chunks, and invokes an internal telemetry event for each chunk. multiplexProperties also creates the full JSON string and Buffer.from input before asynchronous gzip completes. Thus accumulated native reasoning or an image payload is repeatedly processed after headers arrive but before the stream can be consumed.
Findings.Recommendation: Keep the richer telemetry, but hand the Response back and establish stream consumption first; schedule conversion and sendEngineMessagesTelemetry off that critical path (with explicit error handling), or otherwise bound/prepare telemetry before this response-start boundary.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The thinking-only trigger, expanded payload, synchronous helper work, and send-before-emit ordering are directly traced. Magnitude depends on reasoning length, but the latency mechanism is certain.
Findings.PerformanceResource: CPU work, retained and serialized strings, telemetry event objects, and temporary buffers
Findings.PerformanceScaling: For responses containing thinking, synchronous completion-time work grows with answer plus thinking/signature/redacted bytes and creates one internal telemetry event per 8,000 serialized characters.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Increased completion/tool-loop latency and CPU/GC pressure for reasoning-heavy Anthropic responses.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The streaming Messages path sent only rawMessageToCAPI(completion.message), which contains the surfaced answer/tool result, before emitting the completion.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The added telemetryMessages assignment attaches the reconstructed provider content—including full thinking, signature, and redacted blocks—to the completion; the endpoint then synchronously processes that expanded payload before feed.emitOne.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 1422 installs the full native content array whenever a thinking block exists. At unchanged lines 737-739, sendEngineMessagesTelemetry runs before feed.emitOne; the non-streaming branch introduced the same expanded payload and ordering at lines 1059-1079.
Findings.Title: Release Anthropic completions before processing native thinking
Findings.Impact: When Claude emits substantial thinking, users and agent loops wait after message_stop while hidden telemetry content is hashed and split into events; repeated reasoning model calls compound the delay.
Findings.Evidence: sendEngineMessagesTelemetry synchronously adds metadata and serializes the complete array, then sendIndividualMessagesTelemetry recursively hashes every string, serializes each message again, splits it into 8K chunks, and invokes an internal event for each chunk. The new content array includes provider thinking that was previously excluded, so long reasoning now extends the completion-critical path. The default chat processor in this PR demonstrates that completion delivery can remain immediate while telemetry waits until stream completion.
Findings.Recommendation: Emit the completion before scheduling native-content telemetry, and apply the same deferred ordering to the non-streaming branch. Keep the captured content alive only until the deferred telemetry task has taken ownership.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed payload, synchronous serialization/hash path, and send-before-emit ordering are explicit in production code. Only the precise duration for a given model output is uncertain.
Findings.PerformanceResource: CPU work, large serialized strings, telemetry event objects, and temporary buffers
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Cost grows with provider reasoning/content bytes: the payload is traversed for classification, full-array JSON serialization, recursive hashing, per-message JSON serialization, and 8K event chunking before the completion is emitted.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Higher terminal-response latency, CPU/GC pressure, and delayed progress to the next tool or model call.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Responses completions exposed only completion.message to output telemetry, so this pre-emission telemetry path processed the visible answer rather than provider-native reasoning, summaries, encrypted state, and other output items.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The added telemetryMessages field retains the entire normalized provider output, including hidden reasoning and opaque fields, and sendCompletionOutputTelemetry synchronously processes it before feed.emitOne(completion).
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 1510 adds responseApiInputToTelemetryMessages(normalizedOutput) to every completed Responses result; processResponseFromChatEndpoint calls sendCompletionOutputTelemetry at line 1033 and only emits that completion at line 1034.
Findings.Title: Release Responses completions before serializing retained reasoning
Findings.Impact: Reasoning-heavy Responses calls stall completion delivery after the model has already finished. In agent workflows this delays tool execution or the next model iteration on every affected call, with larger stalls as reasoning/output size grows.
Findings.Evidence: sendCompletionOutputTelemetry forwards telemetryMessages to sendEngineMessagesTelemetry. That helper synchronously classifies and JSON.stringify's the array, hashes all message fields character-by-character for deduplication, JSON.stringify's each new message, splits it into 8K chunks, and invokes model.message.added per chunk. Both HTTP and the websocket callback call this telemetry helper before emitting the completion. Hidden reasoning can be much larger than the final answer, so the diff materially increases work at the terminal completion boundary rather than merely passing metadata through.
Findings.Recommendation: Preserve telemetryMessages, but emit the ChatCompletion first and defer output telemetry until after delivery, following the defaultChatResponseProcessor pattern added in this PR; ensure deferred failures remain best-effort and do not affect completion semantics.

Scenarios.Scenario: HTTP Responses API request startup and streaming
Scenarios.CriticalPath: postRequest receives the model HTTP response, but its Promise cannot return the Response to chatMLFetcher and start processResponseFromChatEndpoint/body consumption until the input-telemetry finally handler completes its synchronous conversion, classification, JSON serialization, hashing, and event chunking. Async gzip completion is off the critical path, but creation of the JSON and gzip input buffer is not.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Existing model HTTP request and streamed response body
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One model request/response per model call; unchanged by the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same network request occurred, but telemetry converted reasoning to a short placeholder and omitted compaction/image-generation items before releasing the Response.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Response headers have arrived, but response-body consumption is delayed by the changed synchronous telemetry preparation in Promise.finally.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Convert full Responses history, classify it, JSON-serialize it, hash every message, and split new messages into 8K telemetry chunks
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Every request converts and hashes every effective history item; one enhanced engine payload per call and one internal model.message.added event per 8K chunk of each cache-miss message.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The telemetry path existed but processed compact logging messages; full native reasoning, opaque compaction, and generated-image payloads were absent.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs before the postRequest Promise settles and therefore delays stream startup and first-token handling.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One enhanced engine.messages event plus per-new-message 8K internal chunks; payload/event cardinality grows with newly retained content.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The sinks existed, but received the smaller logging representation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Event calls and property cloning occur synchronously; actual enhanced gzip/send completion is asynchronous.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Complete effective request history after Responses conversion: all user/assistant/tool items plus newly retained native reasoning, compaction state, and image-generation results. Existing messages are deduplicated only after a full-content hash; new messages fan out by serialized size in 8K chunks.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The conversion, classification, JSON serialization, hashing, and internal event creation are serial on the extension-host event loop. gzip is delegated to the libuv threadpool; concurrent model requests can enqueue independent compression jobs without a shared coalescer.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: messageHashToUuid is an LRU positive cache for individual internal events. A warm hit suppresses re-emitting model.message.added but does not suppress conversion, metadata construction, full recursive hashing, engine.messages serialization, or gzip preparation. There is no coalescing or negative-cache state for the input telemetry task.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: Promise.finally ordering, stream-start call flow, data expansion, synchronous hash implementation, and 8K chunk fan-out are directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact added milliseconds depend on conversation length, model reasoning volume, images, telemetry opt-in/sink implementation, and V8/string behavior. Long agent histories and opaque reasoning make the scaling input realistic even though prevalence at the largest sizes is uncertain.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable: the diff materially expands synchronous telemetry work after headers but before response streaming can begin.

Scenarios.Scenario: Responses API terminal output over HTTP and WebSocket
Scenarios.CriticalPath: At response.completed/incomplete/failed, the processor constructs provider-native telemetryMessages. Both the HTTP SSE parser and WebSocket callback call sendCompletionOutputTelemetry before emitting ChatCompletion, so synchronous metadata classification, full-array serialization, recursive hashing, per-message serialization, and internal chunk events must finish before consumers can finalize the answer, run tools, or continue the agent loop.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Consume the existing model SSE/WebSocket response
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One stream per model call, one terminal completion in the normal single-choice scenario.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Terminal output was emitted after telemetry for only the surfaced completion.message.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The model stream has already delivered its terminal event; progress is then blocked by synchronous telemetry work before completion emission.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Convert native output, classify, stringify, recursively hash, re-stringify, and chunk it
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: All native output items are traversed; cache-miss messages produce ceil(serializedLength/8000) internal chunks.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Only the surfaced answer/tool completion was processed; provider-native reasoning and opaque output were not included.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Directly precedes feed/emitter.emitOne on both HTTP and WebSocket paths.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One enhanced event plus per-8K internal events, now scaling with retained hidden output.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same event families with substantially smaller output content.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous preparation/dispatch calls delay completion; actual enhanced compression/send resolves later.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Normalized provider output bytes, especially hidden reasoning content, summaries, encrypted state, images, and number of output items. Internal event cardinality is one per 8K serialized chars for each new message.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Terminal processing is serial in the parser/callback. Enhanced compression continues asynchronously after Buffer creation; internal event creation is synchronous. Separate model calls may overlap but have no shared limiter at this helper.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Individual message UUIDs use the LRU cache, but every output is still recursively hashed and engine.messages is always serialized. Output request IDs generally make these cache keys unique, so warm-cache suppression is limited. gzip has no result cache or coalescing.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: added telemetryMessages, synchronous helper internals, and send-before-emit ordering are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The exact latency depends on provider output size and sink cost. Reasoning-heavy agent calls make the mechanism recurrent; the largest image/opaque payloads are less common.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable: richer output is processed on the terminal completion critical path instead of after delivery.

Scenarios.Scenario: Anthropic Messages API streaming and non-streaming completion
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Streaming accumulates provider content during SSE and, at message_stop, attaches native thinking to telemetryMessages. The endpoint synchronously processes it before feed.emitOne. Non-streaming parses the existing HTTP body, constructs the expanded telemetry payload, processes it, and only then emits the completion.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Existing Anthropic SSE or JSON response
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One network response per model call; one completion in the supported Messages scenario.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same response was processed, with thinking excluded from output telemetry.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Network completion has occurred, but completion delivery waits for telemetry preparation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Reconstruct native blocks, classify, stringify, recursively hash, stringify per message, and split into 8K chunks
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One full native message when thinking exists; ceil(serializedLength/8000) internal events on a cache miss.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Only rawMessageToCAPI(completion.message), excluding thinking/redacted blocks, entered this path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs before feed.emitOne in both streaming and non-streaming branches.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One enhanced event and per-8K internal events; expanded by thinking bytes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Existing events carried only the surfaced output.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Preparation and event calls are synchronous even though enhanced compression/send continues asynchronously.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Answer text plus thinking text, signatures, redacted data, block count, and serialized size. Event count grows by one internal event per 8K chars for a new message.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One Anthropic processor per request; block accumulation and completion telemetry are serial. Compression is asynchronous, but synchronous conversion/hash/chunking is unbounded by a scheduler. Parallel model calls create independent work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The model-message LRU can suppress repeated internal events only after hashing all content. New request IDs and native outputs usually miss. engine.messages serialization and gzip preparation always occur; there is no content compression cache.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the thinking trigger, full content array, synchronous helper path, and ordering are directly visible.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Reasoning length and telemetry sink overhead vary by model and user task. The trigger is limited to messages containing thinking, but those are exactly the reasoning-model scenarios introduced by this telemetry preservation.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable: native thinking materially amplifies synchronous completion-time telemetry work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Default Chat Completions streaming with trailing reasoning and multiple choices
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Finished choices are emitted immediately while the stream continues. Output telemetry is retained until the async iterable finishes, then sent from finally, so it is off the first-completion critical path but still on stream cleanup/completion. Expected choice cardinality is normally one and explicitly two for remote-agent/multi-choice cases.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One stream per request, normally one choice and at most two in traced production overrides.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Completion telemetry was sent immediately per choice and therefore omitted metadata arriving after finish_reason.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Trailing metadata keeps the network stream active, but completed choices are emitted before it; telemetry waits until stream termination.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Accumulate reasoning fields and serialize one telemetry message per completed choice
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One retained reasoning object and one output telemetry call per effective choice.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No provider-native reasoning accumulator for restricted output telemetry.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Accumulation occurs per chunk, but final telemetry serialization is deferred beyond immediate completion delivery.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Reasoning bytes per effective choice and at most the configured expected choices; tests and production routing establish one or two choices in relevant paths.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One SSE processor serializes chunks per stream. Choices share the stream; pending telemetry is flushed serially after the stream ends. Parallel requests remain independent.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Output telemetry uses the same LRU UUID cache, full hashing, and uncached engine serialization. No stream-level coalescing beyond one pending telemetry record per completion choice.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for mechanism and bounded cardinality; lower concern for user-visible magnitude because the critical-path tradeoff is explicitly handled.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Very long reasoning increases retained bytes and per-chunk concatenation work, but choice count is bounded in traced callers and the most important completion delivery is intentionally not blocked.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding: retention is bounded by the stream and effective choice count, and the PR deliberately defers telemetry to preserve completion responsiveness.

Scenarios.Scenario: Conversation message-text telemetry in the extension and Agent Host
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Extension calls send standard telemetry synchronously, then starts restricted multiplex/compression in a fire-and-forget async task. Agent Host user/model message event handlers also invoke reporter methods with void and do not await gzip, so conversation and agent progress do not wait for compression.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: gzip and base64 encode messageText, preserving an 8192-character raw prefix
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One compression per non-empty restricted message event, including short messages.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Extension sent raw messageText directly; Agent Host did not always produce the compressed chunk family for short messageText.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the extension and Agent Host message-processing critical paths due to fire-and-forget callers; Buffer creation occurs when the async task starts but not before the caller returns in the extension wrapper.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send enhanced GH and internal MSFT conversation.messageText telemetry
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two destinations per message using the same multiplexed properties; unchanged destination count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same restricted destinations, with raw/truncated or inconsistently chunked content.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Telemetry sends occur after async compression and are not awaited by product message handlers.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One prompt or assistant message string per emitted conversation message; compressed chunks scale with gzip output up to the existing 50-property cap.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: gzip uses the libuv threadpool. Multiple messages may enqueue independent jobs without explicit coalescing or a custom limiter, but normal cardinality is one user and one model event per turn/model message.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: There is no compression cache; short and long messageText values are always gzip-compressed. Each event performs a fresh compression. This is intentional schema uniformity and remains off the interaction critical path.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: call sites explicitly discard the reporter promises and the extension launches an unawaited async task.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Threadpool pressure could vary under unusually high parallel agent activity, but realistic per-turn cardinality is low and no important workflow awaits completion.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: always-compress adds work but it is bounded per message and kept off the user/agent critical path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Agent Host restricted telemetry routing and prompt/message chunk preservation
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Router/sender multiplexing must finish before the individual telemetry route method completes, but callers of conversation text telemetry are fire-and-forget. Request-options telemetry may await multiplexing only for telemetry completion, not model execution.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: gzip/base64 and property chunking for prompt/messageText/messagesJson
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One gzip operation per forced-compression property; compressed data is represented in up to 50 properties.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: messageText and prompt were not always compressed when below the property limit.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Not on model/message progression for traced prompt/model message callers.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: POST restricted telemetry envelopes to enhanced/internal sinks
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing event/destination count; chunking increases properties/bytes, not POST count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same sinks with less complete prompt/message content.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Telemetry sender is fire-and-forget and failures are logged; product workflows do not await the POST.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Raw prompt/message/tools JSON length and compressed chunk count, capped at 50 properties of 8192 characters.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Compression runs in the shared libuv threadpool with no explicit application limiter; sink dispatch occurs after each compression. Event cardinality remains one routed envelope per destination rather than one envelope per chunk because chunks are properties.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No gzip cache or coalescing; every routed prompt/message event compresses independently. Raw-prefix and compressed family keys are deterministic.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for compression and caller scheduling; medium for deployment-wide parallelism.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Aggregate threadpool/network byte impact depends on parallel sessions and message compressibility, but no realistic high-frequency hot path or critical-path blocking was established.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: increased telemetry bytes/CPU are intentional, capped, and asynchronous with respect to important product progress.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass across all 23 changed files. Reported three materially amplified serialization/allocation regressions: expanded Responses input telemetry blocks HTTP stream startup, and expanded Responses/Anthropic output telemetry blocks terminal completion delivery. Examined trailing-reasoning retention, token-chunk accumulation, message compression, cache/dedup behavior, effective choice counts, libuv compression concurrency, and telemetry boundary cardinality; those remaining mechanisms did not meet the reportable regression threshold.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
